Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — Reports August ISM Services PMI data
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sept 15-16 Fed meeting rate hike probability, August payrolls release imminent
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
August ISM Services PMI beat expectations at 55.4 (vs. 54.2 forecast), with new orders surging to a 3.5-year high of 60.9. Input prices accelerated to 72.6, keeping inflation well above the Fed's 2% target. Demand is being fueled partly by AI spending but supply chains remain stretched, compounded by tariff pressures and the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran. Markets are pricing a ~64% probability of a 25bps rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, with the current rate at 3.50%-3.75%. Services employment remains soft (sub-index 47.8), flagging downside risk to Friday's payrolls print, with consensus at +56K after July's -23K surprise.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — Directly addresses ISM Services, inflation dynamics, Fed rate path, and market-implied probabilities.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (strongly yes — rate hike at Sep meeting is the central narrative)
Probability of increase: 64% (as per CME FedWatch cited in the article)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (weak labor market signals and soft employment sub-index introduce a minor hold narrative)
Probability of holding: 36% (residual from the 64% hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no cut discussion whatsoever)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (More hawkish than before — PMI beat, new orders at 3.5-year high, input prices accelerating, Fed Chair Warsh signaling "work to do," 64% market-implied hike probability all point decisively hawkish; the only offset is weak employment, which is insufficient to shift the overall tone)
